policy: One-off replacement concept batch requested in place of today's Zuzu extras. Do not pretend these are v3 Daily Dream zuzu_assets or overwrite the existing canonical six-linked-world proposal. No Kind Robots objects or ArtJobs created by this draft.
roster_preservation: These are additional supporting cast and henchman species; none replaces the protected 48 playable origin-affinity hero identities, Granny Mayhem, Dr. Frog, or Zuzu Koala Assassin.
setting_rules: All Academy students are adults. Each hook must support night patrol choices, faction variation, and one-screen illustrated character-led play.
required_next_steps: Create SPECIES Facets for each of the four species before linking named henchmen, using the real taxonomy endpoint and durable IDs.
Ingest each NPC or henchman through the sanctioned Kind Robots character/content writer with explicit Prom of Doom provenance and dedupe keys.
Queue real portrait, splash and encounter ArtJobs from catalog-backed checkpoints; record all IDs and verify gallery attachment.
Wire first-encounter scenes, choices, replay secrets, and downstream dispatch effects into Prom of Doom; test hero/villain/rogue paths and seeded replay.

characters.name: Madame Afterparty
characters.identity: Imani Calder, the expelled gala architect who now runs midnight disaster drills disguised as celebrity parties
characters.hook: She turns public embarrassment into literal weather: a whispered secret can spawn a ballroom-wide thunderhead. She once saved Comet City by making its mayor the laughingstock of the planet, then lost her license for it.
characters.visual: A colossal lilac ostrich-feather cape over scarred fireproof formalwear; floating mirrored disco moons; storm clouds shaped like flashbulbs; one mascara streak glitters silver.
characters.mechanic: Patrol choices bank or spend Exposure. High Exposure draws crowds and converts witnesses into backup but gives the mastermind a trail to follow.
characters.turn: On day 11 she offers to expose a villain's identity; refusing protects their family but puts the school in danger.
characters.secret: In villain-aligned runs her legendary scandal was a staged evacuation saving thousands, and her supposed blackmail files can become rescue maps.
characters.art: Full-body rooftop gala portrait, furious lightning-lit expression, rescue-in-the-rain illustration, ruined ballroom encounter; optional hurt and joyous portrait states.

characters.name: The Asterisk
characters.identity: Clem Vega, Comet City's nonbinary registrar and former junior hero who can edit reality only through official corrections
characters.role: Records keeper / legal antagonist / reluctant confidant
characters.hook: Any properly filed correction rewrites the public record and reshuffles reality around it, but people remember both versions. Clem is trying to unmake one disastrous graduation and cannot admit which student died in the original.
characters.visual: Impossibly tall accordion filing cabinet worn as a backpack, iridescent correction-fluid gauntlets, a cape made of redacted diplomas, glowing pen suspended above a split eye.
characters.mechanic: The player can correct one mission outcome on a limited bureaucracy clock, sacrificing reputation or a remembered relationship to do it.
characters.turn: A forged transcript can save a sidekick's scholarship or remove a catastrophe warning from the official map.
characters.secret: A hidden scrap-book contradiction points to the principal mastermind as the person who filed the first false graduation record.
characters.art: Registrar fortress scene with inverted stacks of files, moral-choice portrait, reality-rewrite cinematic, alternate villain version.

characters.name: Coach Event Horizon
characters.identity: Ren Park, a retired champion whose prosthetic lower leg contains a caged miniature sun
characters.role: Combat trainer / evacuation commander / romance-disabled adult mentor
characters.hook: Every time Ren sprints, dawn begins early. Their greatest triumph incinerated the finish line and taught them to treat victory as a dangerous substance.
characters.visual: A broad-shouldered coach in a gold-thread track jacket, solar-flare carbon-fiber prosthesis, tinted goggles scored by tiny meteor trails, a whistle trapped inside a magnetic halo.
characters.mechanic: Training improves mobility and rescue odds; overclocking guarantees an escape at the price of major structural damage.
characters.turn: Day 3's double catastrophe can be solved by accepting Ren's costly firebreak plan, but that burns the school's emergency runway.
characters.secret: The leg's miniature star was commissioned by one of the eight mastermind candidates as a hidden countdown.
characters.art: Stadium dawn training splash, sprint silhouette, exhausted infirmary portrait, scorched evacuation tableau.

characters.name: Choir of One
characters.identity: Juno Bell, a former paramedic who hears every unreturned emergency call in Comet City
characters.hook: Juno conducts invisible callers as a thousand-voice choir. Each harmony reveals where someone is trapped, but the loudest note belongs to the next victim unless the team changes the future.
characters.visual: Silver emergency-radio earrings, long cobalt rescue coat lined with glowing handwritten street names, a baton made from a bent ambulance antenna, orbiting translucent mouths.
characters.mechanic: Reveals one hidden mission consequence per night. Spending the signal can save an unseen civilian but makes another dispatch harder.
characters.turn: In week 2 Juno receives a call from tomorrow asking the player to betray a trusted friend.
characters.secret: The supposedly ghostly calls originate from a city-wide emergency simulation planted by the antagonist, with one real call hidden among them.
characters.art: Signal-storm portrait, crowded emergency exchange, alternate hopeful and fearful facial states, rescue cinematic.

characters.name: Pledgebreaker
characters.species_description: Semi-sentient storm stags born when formal invitations are shredded during lightning storms; each carries its inviter's last unspoken promise in its antlers.
characters.hook: Pledgebreaker leads a stampede of wedding-black lightning stags across the football field, demanding a dance invitation before allowing evacuees across.
characters.visual: A six-legged deer the size of a bus, satin lapel pattern in its fur, chandelier antlers wrapped in blue arcs and hundreds of singed RSVP cards.
characters.mechanic: Electric charge scales with broken promises. Players can bargain, destroy the invitations, or ride the herd across the map.
characters.turn: A hero route frees the herd from invitation contracts; villain route can command it but permanently marks the player as an oathbreaker.
characters.secret: One stag remembers a prom invitation issued to a principal villain years before they were born.
characters.art: Species silhouette sheet with three stags, cinematic arena stampede, individual Pledgebreaker portrait.

characters.name: Miss Reflection
characters.species_description: Architectural predators grown in abandoned security cameras; they step out of reflective surfaces and build nests from stolen surveillance footage.
characters.hook: Miss Reflection is a marble-bodied gargoyle whose glass mouth displays the face of whoever fears her most. She offers the player a recording of a crime they have not yet committed.
characters.visual: Winged art-deco gargoyle with an enormous faceted television-glass jaw, polished mirror claws and a stolen graduation cap balanced on a horn.
characters.mechanic: Mirror rooms create false line-of-sight; revealing a secret disables one reflection and arms another.
characters.turn: Publish a recording to unmask a mastermind, or conceal it to protect a classmate's future.
characters.secret: Her original camera filmed the city's founding, where the first catastrophe was deliberately misreported.
characters.art: Species facet plate, hallway of false reflections, close-up villain portrait and shattered-glass defeat state.

characters.name: Standing Ovation
characters.species_description: Balloon-lung parasites hatched from packed award-night confetti cannons; they feed on applause and inflate until the room itself becomes buoyant.
characters.hook: A stadium cheers for Standing Ovation, a skyscraper-high pink-and-gold leech that keeps a whole audience suspended beneath it like a glittering chandelier.
characters.visual: Translucent ribbon-organ body, golden brass mouth shaped like a megaphone, enormous swaying fringe, hundreds of stolen medals embedded in its skin.
characters.mechanic: The louder the praise, the stronger the creature. Players can win quietly, turn the audience against it, or weaponize applause at civilian risk.
characters.turn: A star student asks the player to fake a victory speech to save fans, jeopardizing their own school standing.
characters.secret: The leech has swallowed a recording of the antagonist's first public speech.
characters.art: High-impact stadium key art, species anatomical silhouette, stunned and enraged variants.

characters.name: Lady Hemline
characters.species_description: Enormous theatrical spiders that weave wearable false memories into evening clothes. Their silk can heal trauma or erase accountability depending on the wearer.
characters.hook: Lady Hemline crashes graduation fittings with a wardrobe of impossible dresses. Each lets a student become the person they wish they had been, until the wearer forgets who loved them before.
characters.visual: An eight-limbed spider in a cathedral-sized burgundy bustle, pearl-tipped legs, six dressing-room mirrors orbiting the abdomen, needle-fine blue eyes.
characters.mechanic: A temporary persona swap unlocks an alternate route while risking a lost bond or a scrambled mission memory.
characters.turn: Recover a friend's stolen past, or use a velvet disguise to infiltrate the mastermind's prom-night operation.
characters.secret: A hidden lining contains one unaltered memory of the original city-destruction rehearsal.
characters.art: Grand dressing-room full-body splash, species facet silhouettes, memory-swap effect, alternate rescued and villain-bound forms.
